questions.prompt: A cloud bucket continuously receives new JSON files. What does Auto Loader provide?

options.text: A replacement for destination access permissions
Direct CDC reading of any relational database log
Incremental discovery and processing of new files through the cloudFiles source

questions.prompt: Which property of Delta Lake guarantees that a write either fully succeeds or has no effect, even with concurrent writers?

options.text: ACID transactions backed by optimistic concurrency control
Eventual consistency
At-least-once delivery
Schema-on-read

questions.explanation: Delta Lake provides ACID transactions using optimistic concurrency control on the transaction log. Commits are atomic and isolated, so a write fully succeeds or leaves the table unchanged, even when multiple jobs write concurrently.

questions.prompt: What does the PIVOT operation do in SQL?

options.text: It sorts the data in descending order
It creates a backup of the table
It removes duplicate rows
It rotates data from rows into columns, aggregating values

questions.explanation: PIVOT rotates row values into column headers, typically with aggregation. For example, converting month rows (Jan, Feb, Mar) into columns with SUM(sales) as values. UNPIVOT does the reverse (columns to rows). PIVOT is useful for cross-tab reports and transforming data for analysis.

questions.prompt: A streaming query emits independent, newly arrived records to a compatible sink. Which output mode emits only new result rows?

options.text: Replace mode, which is the standard streaming output mode
Append mode
Update mode, which emits every row on each trigger
Complete mode, which emits the full result table

questions.explanation: Append mode only outputs new rows added to the result table since the last trigger. Complete mode outputs the entire result table. Update mode outputs only rows that were updated. Replace mode does not exist in Structured Streaming. Append is most common for stateless transformations writing to files or Delta tables.

questions.prompt: A JDBC-only source records every insert and update with a strictly increasing change sequence. How should a scheduled notebook ingest it incrementally?

options.text: Use Auto Loader directly against the database transaction log
Read rows above the saved sequence, commit them to Delta, and then advance the saved sequence
Read the first 1,000 rows on every run
Advance the saved sequence before writing the destination

questions.explanation: A high-water mark can limit JDBC reads when the source reliably exposes changes. Advance it after a successful sink commit and make retries idempotent. Timestamp cursors need tie and late-update handling; this pattern does not capture deletes unless the source represents them.

questions.prompt: Which SQL window function assigns the same rank to ties and leaves a gap in later ranks, such as 1, 1, 3?

options.text: union followed by automatic distinct
inner join on every column
unionByName

questions.explanation: unionByName aligns columns by name and preserves duplicates. DataFrame union aligns columns by position and also preserves duplicates. SQL UNION removes duplicates by default; SQL UNION ALL preserves them.

questions.prompt: BI users repeatedly query an expensive aggregate over silver data. They want stored results maintained by refresh, rather than recomputing a virtual view for each query. Which gold object fits?

options.text: A Git folder
A streaming checkpoint directory
A materialized view
A session-only temporary view

questions.explanation: A materialized view stores query results and updates them through refresh processing, which can be incremental when supported. A regular view stores only its query. questions.prompt: Which SQL clause is used to filter rows after aggregation has been performed?

options.text: AGGREGATE
HAVING
WHERE
FILTER

questions.explanation: HAVING filters rows after GROUP BY aggregation, while WHERE filters rows before aggregation. HAVING can reference aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG) in its condition, which WHERE cannot do. This is standard SQL behavior: WHERE filters input rows, HAVING filters grouped results.

questions.prompt: Which approach is recommended for handling slowly changing dimensions (SCD) Type 1 in Delta Lake?

options.text: Delete the entire table and recreate it
Create a new table for each update
Use MERGE INTO with WHEN MATCHED UPDATE to overwrite existing records and WHEN NOT MATCHED INSERT for new records

questions.prompt: What is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT OUTER JOIN?

options.text: LEFT OUTER JOIN is faster than INNER JOIN
INNER JOIN can only be used with two tables
There is no difference; they return the same results
INNER JOIN returns only matching rows from both tables; LEFT OUTER JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right

questions.explanation: INNER JOIN returns only rows that have matching values in both tables. LEFT OUTER JOIN (or LEFT JOIN) returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right; if no match exists, NULL values are returned for right table columns. RIGHT OUTER JOIN and FULL OUTER JOIN follow similar logic for the right table or both tables respectively.
